Hash Utilities

Data Change Tracking Utilities

This module helps track changes in data files by: 1. Computing summaries of data content 2. Generating unique fingerprints (hashes) of those summaries 3. Storing the history of changes 4. Reporting when data has been modified

The goal is to make data changes transparent and traceable, helping maintain data integrity and compliance.

hash_utils.create_fingerprint(summary)[source]

Create a unique fingerprint (hash) of a data summary.

We use SHA256 because: - It’s cryptographically secure - Produces fixed-length output - Even tiny changes result in completely different fingerprints

hash_utils.load_history()[source]

Load the history of data changes from the log file. Returns an empty history if this is the first time.

hash_utils.report_changes(filepath, old_version, new_summary)[source]

Generate a human-readable report of what changed in the data.

Shows: - Which file changed - What the specific changes were - When the change was detected

hash_utils.save_history(history)[source]

Save the updated history of data changes to the log file.

hash_utils.setup_config()[source]

Create or load the configuration settings.

The config file determines whether to use Git for distributed tracking or keep everything local. Default is local-only mode.

hash_utils.share_fingerprint(filepath, fingerprint, config)[source]

Share the data fingerprint with other users.

In Git mode: Pushes to a shared repository In local mode: Saves to a local file

hash_utils.summarize_dataframe(df)[source]

Create a summary of a dataframe’s content.

Instead of tracking every value, we track: - The number of rows - The sum of each numeric column This gives us a good fingerprint of the data while being space-efficient.

The hash_utils module provides utilities for tracking and managing data changes:

  • Data fingerprinting

  • Change history management

  • Configuration handling
